Re-gate (Layer 3, /conexus:rdr-gate), RDR-204, docs/rdr/rdr-204-embedding-profile-and-collection-authority.md, commit 4beaeb367 (eighth pass). Prior gate: T2 [24847] 204-gate-critique-2026-09-07g (PASSED, 0 Critical, 2 Significant, 2 Observations). Fix commits under review: 521daefb8, 4beaeb367 (both from [24847]'s two Significant findings; fix record 204-research-13 [24849]).

## Critique Summary

Both prior Significant findings (research-6 mis-citation, RDR-144 missing from related_rdrs) are genuinely closed. But the fix commits introduce three new, verifiable defects: one stale citation the fix forgot to sweep at a second site making the identical claim, and two factual errors in newly-added glosses (legacy_grandfathered's origin RDR, and model_version's relationship to the name) that self-contradict material already present elsewhere in the same document. All three are documentation/evidentiary-accuracy defects with no build-breaking consequence — the underlying engineering design is unaffected — but they recur the exact "false citation" pattern the last three fix commits have each introduced, and one is the specific "fix the fact everywhere, not just one line" failure mode this project has a standing directive against, named after this very RDR.

## Critical Issues

### Issue: Stale citation not swept — line 473-474 still cites the sources the fix just replaced

- **Location**: Technical Design, step 3 ("The second walks every surviving row" paragraph), line 473-474: "On both censused tenants every two-segment row is a ghost (T2 `204-research-1`, `-6`), so this branch is expected to write nothing."
- **Problem**: This is the SAME factual claim ("every two-segment row is a ghost on both tenants") that commit 4beaeb367 just corrected at two other sites in this document: Critical Assumption 4 (line 319-329) and the Finalization Gate's Assumption Verification (line 750-754), both now correctly cite `204-research-13`. This third occurrence, a few lines below the Critical Assumption it restates, was not updated and still names `204-research-1` (single-tenant only, per the prior gate's own finding) and `204-research-6` (per the prior gate's own finding, does not verify this claim at all — it verifies the one-model-per-content-type premise, a different assumption).
- **Impact**: A reader who reads Critical Assumption 4 (now accurate, citing `-13`) and then reads Technical Design step 3 a few paragraphs later sees the same claim attributed to different, weaker evidence, with no indication the first citation superseded the second. This is precisely the class of defect the project's own standing directive names: "A gate fix changes a fact, not a line: grep the whole RDR for old and new phrasing before re-gating; state each count once and derive lists" (T2 `feedback_fix_the_fact_everywhere_before_regate.md`, sourced from this exact RDR, "two blocked rounds on survivors"). Grep of the whole document for `204-research-1`, `-6`, `-13` (run as part of this pass) confirms this is the only remaining unswept site — the other two `-6` citations (line 302, 583, 750) are for the correctly-still-`-6`-cited assumption 1 (one-model-per-content-type), not this claim.
- **Recommendation**: Change line 473-474 to cite `204-research-13` alone, matching the corrected Critical Assumption 4 wording (e.g., "On both active tenants every two-segment row is a ghost (T2 `204-research-13`), so this branch is expected to write nothing.").
- **Evidence**: `grep -n "204-research-1\b\|204-research-6\|204-research-13"` on the current file; T2 [24847] Significant 1 (the finding that motivated the -13 census and the two citation fixes); T2 `204-research-13` [24849].
- **Ship-blocker**: no — cosmetic within a draft; does not affect the backfill's actual behavior (which correctly has a fallback rule for a two-segment row that does carry vectors regardless of which research entry is cited).

### Issue: legacy_grandfathered misattributed to RDR-103; contradicts this RDR's own Relationship table

- **Location**: Research Findings, Key Discoveries, line 216-217 (added by 521daefb8): "All 22 `legacy_grandfathered` rows (the flag RDR-103 set on rows registered before its naming shape, so they are readable but exempt from the conformance check) are ghosts."
- **Problem**: `legacy_grandfathered` is RDR-101's flag, not RDR-103's. Three independent sources confirm this: (a) this RDR's own Relationship table, row for RDR-101 (line 121): "Created `catalog_collections` as a 'first-class collections projection' (changeset catalog-001-5)" — `catalog-001-5` in `catalog-001-baseline.xml` is the changeset that creates the `legacy_grandfathered` column (`legacy_grandfathered INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, line 207); (b) RDR-101's own text (`docs/rdr/rdr-101-catalog-t3-metadata-design.md:165`): `bool legacy_grandfathered "true for pre-RDR-101 collection names"`, and line 323: "Legacy two-segment names ... are grandfathered via the projection's `legacy_grandfathered` flag"; (c) RDR-103's own text (`docs/rdr/rdr-103-catalog-collection-name-authority.md:172`) explicitly attributes the invariant elsewhere: "Legacy collection names remain valid T3 strings and remain readable per RDR-101 Phase 6's grandfathering invariant" — RDR-103 never claims to have set the flag itself; it only builds `is_conformant_collection_name` as a bridge that reads the naming shape RDR-101's Phase 6 amendment defined.
- **Impact**: This RDR's own Relationship table (unchanged by these two commits, per the task's framing) already states catalog-001-5 is RDR-101's; the new gloss at line 216-217 contradicts it two pages later, in the same document. A reader relying on the newly-added gloss (the whole point of adding it, per Criterion 6) is told a fact the RDR's own earlier table disproves.
- **Recommendation**: Change "the flag RDR-103 set" to "the flag RDR-101 set" at line 216-217. (`catalog-031-3-collections-legacy-bool`, RDR-unrelated hygiene work, later converted the column's type from INTEGER to boolean — that detail, if kept, is accurate and can stay.)
- **Evidence**: `docs/rdr/rdr-101-catalog-t3-metadata-design.md:165,323`; `docs/rdr/rdr-103-catalog-collection-name-authority.md:172`; `service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/catalog-001-baseline.xml:196-215` (changeset `catalog-001-5`, author `nexus-gmiaf.18`); `service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/catalog-031-type-hygiene.xml:217-242` (`catalog-031-3-collections-legacy-bool`, INTEGER→boolean). T2 `204-research-13` [24849] carries the identical misattribution in its "part 1" gloss line and should be corrected there too (not edited by this critique, per read-only instructions).
- **Ship-blocker**: no — purely an attribution error in explanatory prose; the exemption behavior itself (readable, excluded from conformance check) is correctly described.

### Issue: model_version's relationship to the name is stated backwards and contradicts this RDR's own Research Finding

- **Location**: Technical Design, step 3, line 460-463 (added by 521daefb8): "The columns the name never carried (`model_version`, `display_name`, `superseded_by`, `superseded_at`) are left exactly as registered: `model_version` is supplied by the client at registration and upserted by the engine, never parsed from the name, so the walk does not touch it."
- **Problem**: `model_version` is grouped with three columns the name genuinely never encodes (`display_name`, `superseded_by`, `superseded_at`), but `model_version` IS the name's fourth segment for every conformant (four-segment) collection: the name format is `<content_type>__<owner_id>__<embedding_model>__v<n>`, and `v<n>` is `model_version` — confirmed by `CollectionName.render()` (`f"...__v{self.model_version}"`) and `CollectionName.parse()` / `parse_conformant_collection_name()` (`model_version=f"v{g['ver']}"` / `int(parsed["model_version"][1:])`), `src/nexus/catalog/collection_name.py:92,139` and `src/nexus/corpus.py:148`. "Never parsed from the name" is also false as a general claim: `src/nexus/indexer.py:797` sets `model_version=segments["model_version"]` where `segments` comes from parsing the just-rendered name (`parse_conformant_collection_name`) — and this is the EXACT call site this RDR's own Research Findings, line 254-257, already cites and verifies: "registration derives a collection's attributes by parsing the name it has just rendered (`indexer.py:785-800`)." The same parse-from-name pattern recurs at `src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/collections.py:129,339`, `src/nexus/commands/collection.py:728`, `src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/migration.py:186`, and `HttpCatalogClient.collection_for` (`src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:2762`, `CollectionName.parse(result["name"]).model_version`) — the very client class this RDR's Technical Environment section names.
- **Impact**: Direct self-contradiction — the same document verifies (Research Findings) that registration parses the rendered name for its attributes, then two pages later (Technical Design) claims model_version specifically is "never parsed from the name." The narrower, defensible claim — that the ENGINE's Java code never splits the name string to derive `model_version` (it only trusts whatever value the client's HTTP call supplied, confirmed by `CatalogRepository`'s upsert using `DSL.excluded(CATALOG_COLLECTIONS.MODEL_VERSION)` with no string-splitting) — IS true and is presumably what this sentence meant, but as written it overclaims into an ontological statement about the name itself ("the columns the name never carried") that is false for `model_version` specifically.
- **Recommendation**: Split `model_version` out of the "columns the name never carried" list (keep only `display_name`, `superseded_by`, `superseded_at` there). State the narrower, true claim separately: something like "`model_version` already carries a value for every conformant row, set at original registration when the client parses the rendered name's own `v<n>` segment (`indexer.py:797`); the ENGINE never re-derives it from the name during the walk — it only ever takes the client-supplied value (`CatalogRepository`'s upsert, `DSL.excluded(MODEL_VERSION)`) — so the walk leaves it untouched."
- **Evidence**: `src/nexus/catalog/collection_name.py:60,92,139`; `src/nexus/corpus.py:100-148` (`parse_conformant_collection_name`); `src/nexus/indexer.py:770-800`; `src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:2650-2700` (`register_collection`), `:2730-2777` (`collection_for`, `CollectionName.parse(result["name"]).model_version`); `src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/collections.py:129,339`; `src/nexus/commands/collection.py:728`; `src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/migration.py:186`; `service/.../CatalogRepository.java:6178-6220,6969-6995,8217-8277` (MODEL_VERSION upsert via `DSL.excluded`); RDR-204's own Research Findings, line 254-257.
- **Ship-blocker**: no — the underlying design (walk leaves model_version as registered) is sound and does not depend on the false justification; no NOT NULL/non-empty constraint is added on `model_version` (Technical Design step 2's constraint list omits it), so nothing in Phase 1's implementation steps actually requires the false claim to be true.

## Significant Issues

None.

## Observations

- **Key Discoveries' "45 four-segment" ghost count (line 214-215, unchanged, from the 2026-09-06 census) differs from what `204-research-13`'s 2026-09-07T17:26:57Z numbers imply for the same tenant** (115 four-segment rows, 71 with chunks/stats -> 44 ghosts, not 45). This is not a contradiction: research-13's own finding 2 explains it ("nexus has 71 stats rows, one more than research-6's 70 at 00:35Z; a new collection was indexed in between"), and the two figures carry different timestamps that the document does not claim to reconcile. No fix needed; noting it so a future pass doesn't mistake it for fresh drift.
- Criterion 6 (WARN, outside-reader readability): all three terms the seventh gate flagged as undefined (`legacy_grandfathered`, `model_version`, `catalog_meta`) now carry inline glosses at first use — the readability gap itself is closed. Two of the three glosses are factually wrong (Critical Issues 2 and 3 above); that is a content-accuracy defect, not a remaining readability gap. No other undefined or forward-referenced terms found in a fresh scan of the document (bead ids, `MODEL_DIMS`, `PITR fork`, `grandfather-or-raise`, `COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES`, `dormant`/`disputed`/`live`/`quarantine` lifecycle states — all glossed at or before first use).
- `204-research-13` [24849] itself carries the same legacy_grandfathered/RDR-103 misattribution as the RDR (Critical Issue 2) in its "part 1" summary line. Its own closing claim — "every factual sentence in both commits was read from its source ... nothing in them is from memory" — is contradicted by this specific sentence, which does not check out against RDR-101 or RDR-103's own text.
